title: Application spec (V2 WS1 requirements intake)
description: The contract everything downstream verifies against: requirement -> ambiguity detection -> clarifying questions -> spec lock. Mirrors generation/spec.py::ApplicationSpec.to_dict(). THE RULE (V2_PLAN 4b(b)): never invent a requirement — ask. Every user-supplied value is a provenancedValue whose provenance is 'user' (the human stated it, with the verbatim span quoted in `evidence`) or 'asked' (the human answered a clarifying question). There is deliberately NO 'inferred'/'model'/'default' — a value that cannot be grounded in something the user said is not a value, it is an entry in open_questions. This is generation/inputs.py's V1.6 provenance gate at application scale. A spec is only buildable when assert_spec_complete() passes, which requires zero blocking open_questions; no spec line => no code.

requirement_text.description: The user's own words, accumulated across the intake conversation. Every `evidence` span on a 'user'-provenanced value must occur verbatim in here — that is what makes the spec auditable.

target.description: Board and MCU. Both are required and neither is ever derived from the other: 'Nucleo-F411RE' does not auto-fill the MCU part, because that inference is exactly the silent auto-fill V1.6 killed.

devices.description: The composed devices. Deliberately shaped close to the device dicts validator/resource_crosscheck.py consumes, so the spec feeds the resource map with no translation layer in between that could invent a pin or an address.

name.description: An orderable part number (BME280, SSD1306), not a category. A category ('a temp sensor') is an ambiguous_chip question, never resolved to a part on the user's behalf.

interface.description: value is one of I2C, SPI, GPIO, ANALOG, UART, 1-WIRE.

address.description: 7-bit bus address, only when the user stated one; otherwise it comes from the device datasheet downstream, never from here.

pin.description: Required for GPIO/ANALOG devices — a pin-less GPIO device cannot be resource-checked.

behaviors.description: trigger -> action. 'when temperature is above 30 C, turn the relay on'. These are what the WS5 emulation run asserts against.

comparator.description: value is one of >, >=, <, <=, ==, !=. Grounded from the user's own words ('above' -> '>'), never chosen for them.

threshold.description: value is a number. A behavior with no stated number is a missing_threshold question, never a plausible default.

constraints.description: Named non-functional values (sample_rate, timeout, baud_rate). `name` is this project's vocabulary key, so it carries no provenance; `value` and `unit` are the user's and do.

failure_behavior.description: What the application does when a device read fails. Required: silently choosing 'log and continue' would be inventing a safety decision.

output_target.description: The artifact to produce: arduino-sketch | platformio-project | cmake-project (free text is accepted and echoed back).

open_questions.description: Everything still ambiguous, as specific answerable questions. Recomputed deterministically by detect_ambiguities(); assert_spec_complete() recomputes rather than trusting this list, so clearing it does not buy permission to build.

dropped.description: Audit trail of values the model produced that could NOT be grounded in the user's text and were therefore discarded in favour of a question. This is the honesty receipt: 'the model wanted to say BME280; we refused and asked'.

provenance.description: 'user' = stated in the requirement text, with `evidence` quoting the exact span. 'asked' = the human answered a clarifying question, with `evidence` naming the question id and the answer. No other value exists, by design.

evidence.description: The receipt. For 'user' it is a verbatim span of requirement_text (checked mechanically, so a fabricated quote is rejected before the value is read). For 'asked' it is 'answer to <question id>: <answer>'. A value with no evidence is an invented value.

field.description: Dotted path of the field this answers: target.board, devices[0].interface, behaviors[0].trigger.threshold, constraints.sample_rate.

kind.description: Ambiguity class. 'model_proposed' questions come from the LLM: they are screened for specificity, may only be added for a field already unknown, and are non-blocking — the model can surface nuance but can never hold generation hostage or set a value.

text.description: The question itself: specific and answerable in one line ('Which I2C address is the BME280 strapped to?'), never vague ('Any other details?').

options.description: Only ever drawn from a closed vocabulary this project owns (interfaces, comparators, output targets). Never a suggested part number, board or threshold — a suggestion is an invented value wearing a question mark.

blocking.description: True = assert_spec_complete() refuses to let generation start until it is answered. No spec line => no code.
